newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moskvich fires chief, still in Renault talks.
newsitem.headline: Moskvich fires chief, still in Renault talks.

text.p: Troubled Russian car maker AO Moskvich has replaced its chief executive but is still in talks with France's Renault to build cars in Russia, a top company official said on Wednesday.

Technical Director Ruben Asatryan was made acting chief executive of the company on November 29. The company stopped production of its popular Moskvich small passenger car earlier this year, said Yuri Polyakov, first deputy director.
But he said discussions with Renault, which former chief executive Yuri Borodin led in France last week, were still on.
"Why would they be changed?" he said. He declined to give details of the talks and a reason for the management move, though the company is in financial difficulty.
Moskvich has been idle since earlier this year when it stopped the production lines of its Moskvich, also known as Aleko, cars, which are popular in Moscow but have a poor reputation for endurance.
The Federal Bankruptcy Authority began bankruptcy proceedings in late October, when the government said Moskvich owed 271 billion roubles ($49 million) in tax arrears.

A spokeswoman for the French car maker said by telephone from Paris that talks were still underway between Renault and Moskvich to build Renault's Megane cars in Moscow, though no agreement had been reached.
"Nothing has been signed. It is just talk," she said.
She said financing for a separate February 1996 deal to sell up to 40,000 Renault engines a year to Moskvich was expected to be approved shortly by commercial banks that she did not name.
"We will probably start to sell engines to Moskvich next year," she said.

In June President Boris Yeltsin decreed unnamed federal support for Moskvich, a big employer in the Russian capital, as well as payment of government debts to Moskvich of at least 100 billion roubles.
Borodin had been named director for growth, his office said.
